title: The American Civil War
key_facts: Fought between the Northern states (Union) and the Southern states (Confederacy).
The bloodiest conflict in American history.
Resulted in the abolition of slavery in the United States.
The Battle of Gettysburg was a turning point in the war.
causes: Long-standing disagreement over the institution of slavery.
Debates over states' rights versus federal authority.
Economic differences between the industrial North and the agrarian South.
The election of Abraham Lincoln in 1860.
outcome: Victory for the Union and preservation of the United States.
Abolition of slavery with the 13th Amendment.

figures.name: Abraham Lincoln
figures.significance: Led the Union during the war and issued the Emancipation Proclamation.

figures.name: Ulysses S. Grant
figures.role: Commanding General of the Union Army
figures.significance: Led the Union Army to victory over the Confederacy.

figures.name: Robert E. Lee
figures.significance: Commanded the Army of Northern Virginia.

figures.name: Jefferson Davis
figures.significance: Leader of the Confederacy during the war.

impacts: Ended the institution of slavery in the United States.
Strengthened the power of the federal government.
Left deep social and political scars that influenced the Reconstruction era and beyond.
sources: McPherson, J. M. (1988). Battle Cry of Freedom: The Civil War Era.
Library of Congress. (n.d.). The Civil War.
